sections.heading: Introduction to File Handling
sections.content:
File handling allows programs to permanently store data on disk and retrieve it later. Python provides built-in functions for working with files.

Types of files in Python:
• Text files (.txt, .csv, .py) — store data as readable characters
• Binary files (.jpg, .mp3, .dat) — store data as bytes

sections.heading: Opening and Closing Files
sections.content:
Use the open() built-in function to open a file. Always close files after use to free system resources.

File modes:
• 'r' — read (default)
• 'w' — write (creates or truncates)
• 'a' — append
• 'x' — exclusive creation
• 'rb', 'wb' — read/write binary

codeBlocks.code:
# Method 1: Manual open/close
f = open('notes.txt', 'w')
f.write('Hello, World!')
f.close()

# Method 2: with statement (recommended)
with open('notes.txt', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
print(content)  # Hello, World!
# File is automatically closed after the with block
codeBlocks.explanation: Always prefer the 'with' statement — it automatically closes the file even if an exception occurs.

sections.heading: Reading from Files
sections.content:
Python provides three methods to read from a text file:

• read() — reads the entire file as a single string
• readline() — reads one line at a time
• readlines() — reads all lines into a list

codeBlocks.code:
# Suppose data.txt contains:
# Line 1
# Line 2
# Line 3

with open('data.txt', 'r') as f:
    # Read all lines into a list
    lines = f.readlines()
    for line in lines:
        print(line.strip())  # strip() removes trailing newline
codeBlocks.explanation: Each line in readlines() includes the newline character '\n'. Use strip() to remove it.

sections.heading: CSV File Handling
sections.content: CSV (Comma Separated Values) files store tabular data with commas separating values. Python's csv module makes reading/writing CSV files simple.

codeBlocks.code:
import csv

# Writing a CSV file
data = [['Name', 'Marks'], ['Asha', 95], ['Rohan', 88]]
with open('students.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f)
    writer.writerows(data)

# Reading a CSV file
with open('students.csv', 'r') as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)
    for row in reader:
        print(row)
codeBlocks.explanation: newline='' is important when writing CSV on Windows to prevent extra blank lines.
